title: Container NVIDIA init error trace (personal notes)
content:
Context:
- Quick personal scratchpad while chasing a reproducible container failure across dev machines and CI.
- Symptoms started after teammates pulled a new base image that upgraded CUDA runtime libraries to 12.x while the host driver is pinned to 535.x.
- Goal: capture commands tried, raw error snippets, hypotheses, and minimal repro steps for a postmortem.

Top-level symptom (most common):
- Container crashes on GPU initialization. App-level stack: NVML init fails or PyTorch throws "CUDA error: initialization error".
- Example runtime error observed:
  nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: nvml: driver/library version mismatch
  OR inside python: torch.cuda.is_available() -> False and import torch; torch.cuda.current_device() -> RuntimeError: CUDA error: initialization error
  OR: ImportError: libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

Environment snapshot (typical host + container mismatch case):
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 5.15.0-71-generic
- Host NVIDIA driver: 535.86.10 (nvidia-smi shows 535.86.10)
- Container base image: nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-cudnn8-runtime-ubuntu22.04 (runtime libs CUDA 12.1)
- Python env: conda py3.10, torch built against CUDA 11.8 wheel (common because wheels lag)

Commands & outputs I ran (useful when pasting into issues):
1) Check host driver / GPU:
  $ nvidia-smi
  +------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 535.86.10    Driver Version: 535.86.10     |
  | GPU 0: Tesla T4 (UUID: GPU-xxxx)                     |
  +------------------------------------------------------+

2) Quick container run reproducer:
  $ docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint /bin/bash nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-cudnn8-runtime-ubuntu22.04 -c \"python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL(\\\"libcudart.so\\\")'\"
  -> Container exit with: \"nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: nvml: driver/library version mismatch\"

3) Inspect libcuda inside container vs host:
  $ docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint /bin/bash nvidia/cuda:12.1.1 -c \"ls -l /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so*; ldconfig -p | grep libcudart\"
  -> In some failing cases libcudart points to 12.x in container but host's libcuda (libcuda.so) is from a driver that expects different ABI.

4) ldd on pytorch's _C.cpython file (inside container venv):
  $ ldd /opt/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep cuda
  -> shows references to libcudart.so.11 and libcuda.so.535 -> mismatch sometimes -> missing soname version -> import fails with undefined symbol errors.

5) Check NVML version mismatch (host):
  $ cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
  NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module  535.86.10  Wed Sep 27 12:34:56 PDT 2023

Observed error fragments (collected):
- \"nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: nvml: driver/library version mismatch\"
- \"NVRM: oslib: 'glibc' unsupported, driver built for different kernel ABI\" (rare)
- \"CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version\"
- \"cannot open shared object file: libcudart.so.11.0: No such file or directory\"
- \"undefined symbol: cuDeviceGetAttribute\" when importing torch -> usually implies mixed libcuda/libcudart table mismatch

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Container runtime ships CUDA runtime libs (cudart) newer than what the host driver supports -> NVML/driver mismatch.
2) nvidia-container-toolkit or nvidia-driver on host is out of date relative to libcuda expected by container images (common after base image bump).
3) LD_LIBRARY_PATH / rpath inside container causes container to pick up host-provided libcuda but container cudart ABI incompatible -> means your container binary expects older soname.
4) PyTorch wheel built for CUDA 11.x loaded inside CUDA 12 runtime container -> wheel/runtime mismatch triggers undefined symbols.
5) Kernel module vs driver userspace mismatch after driver update failed partially -> leads to nvml refusing connections.

Things I tried to confirm & fix (notes and results):
- Try forcing container image with matching CUDA runtime: switch to nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime -> test app runs. (Outcome: success in local repro, confirms runtime mismatch hypothesis).
- On host, sudo apt install --reinstall nvidia-driver-535 -> reloaded modules, nvidia-smi regained consistent NVML output. (Outcome: temporarily fixed on one host)
- Run docker with --gpus all but also mount /usr/local/nvidia/lib64 into container to force host libs -> produced lib mismatch / undefined symbols (bad idea).
- ldd of python binding -> showed missing symbols from libcudart.so.11; replaced container base to 11.8 and import succeeded.
- Upgraded nvidia-container-toolkit to latest stable (post-2024 releases add better diagnostics). After upgrade, error messaging more explicit (gave \"driver/library version mismatch\").

Minimal repro steps (to reproduce the failure cleanly):
1) Host driver = 535.x (older than what your container's cudart needs)
2) Pull base image with CUDA 12.x (nvidia/cuda:12.1-runtime)
3) Run a python app that imports torch built for CUDA 11.x OR simply try to load libcudart of incompatible major version.
4) Observe \"nvml: driver/library version mismatch\" or \"CUDA driver version is insufficient\".

Quick local checklist / debugging commands (copy/paste):
- Host: nvidia-smi; cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version; uname -a\\- Host: dpkg -l | grep -i nvidia; lsmod | grep nvidia\\- Check container libs: docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint /bin/bash nvidia/cuda:12.1 -c \"ldconfig -p | grep libcuda; ldconfig -p | grep libcudart\"\\- Inside container venv: python -c \"import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so')\" and python -c \"import torch; print(torch.version.cuda)\"\\- ldd binary: ldd $(python -c 'import torch; print(__import__(\"inspect\").getsource(torch.cuda))' 2>/dev/null) (ugh, messy)

Notes about best remediation approaches (so we don't patch in the wrong place):
- Prefer to align container runtime to host driver (e.g., use CUDA 11.8 runtime if host driver is 535.x and supports 11.8).
- If host driver is older, either upgrade driver (system change) or use a container with older runtime libs. For CI, pin base images.
- Avoid bind-mounting /usr/local/nvidia from host into container unless you know ABI surfaces; container's shipped libcudart + host libcuda must be ABI-compatible.
- For PyTorch users: prefer matching torch wheel (CUDA version) to runtime; OR use \"torch._C._cuda_getDeviceCount()\" to early detect failures in startup tests.

Weird corner cases seen: 
- One machine had driver package partially upgraded: nvidia-smi showed new driver, but /proc/driver/nvidia/version showed older date -> reboot needed. After reboot, NVML errors cleared.
- WSL2: different ordering of driver/user libs -> often \"driver/library version mismatch\" until Windows WSL driver updated.
- Multipass VM images on CI sometimes ship with built-in older NVIDIA runtime libs; you must ensure the VM host driver and guest container runtime are synced.

Open TODOs / next steps:
- Create a small repro container that logs both container's libcudart sonames and host libcuda ABI at start and fails with clear error message; attach to GH issue. (Planned PR: runtime/diagnostics addition)
- Add CI job that runs a tiny CUDA probe in a matrix of host drivers vs container images we test for (11.8, 12.1) -> catch regressions when base image bumps.
- Draft a short infra doc: \"How to choose container CUDA runtime vs host driver\" (for internal onboarding).

References & quick links I keep using:
- NVIDIA CUDA compatibility guide (compatibility matrix) - https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/cuda-compatibility/index.html
- nvidia-container-toolkit docs & diagnostic flags - https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/container-toolkit/
- Internal GH: runtime issue #842 (example repro attached)

Notes-to-self: keep this in users/ so I can iterate. If I end up with a polished how-to, move it to shared_drives/engineering/infrastructure or product docs.

Raw copied diagnostic (example) that I pasted into Slack: 
-----BEGIN PASTE-----
Host: Ubuntu 22.04, driver 535.86.10
$ docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.1-runtime python -c \"import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()); import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcudart.so')\"
nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: nvml: driver/library version mismatch
-----END PASTE-----

If I come back to this in 6 months: first check driver vs container major CUDA versions. If mismatch -> update host driver OR pin base image.
